images.title: A projection is never longer
images.purpose: Show that a slanting stick, its projection and the height difference make a right triangle, so the projection is shorter.
images.composition: A side view: a table line, a slanting stick above it, two dropped perpendiculars and the right triangle.
images.exact_structure: A long horizontal dark line near the bottom of the frame, labelled 'table'. Above it, one straight teal #0072B2 stick slanting up to the right, 5 cm long, its lower end higher than the table and its upper end 3 cm higher than the lower end. From each end a dashed grey #6B7280 perpendicular drops to the table, with a small right angle mark at each foot. The segment between the two feet is thick reddish purple #CC79A7 and labelled 'projection 4 cm'. From the lower end of the stick a dashed grey horizontal line runs right to the upper end's perpendicular, forming a right triangle with the stick: the stick is labelled 'stick 5 cm' and the vertical side of the triangle '3 cm', with a right angle mark.

images.takeaway: The stick is the longest side of the right triangle, so its projection is shorter.
